label: Workable
terms_note: Job Board API: public GET <subdomain>.workable.com/api/v1/jobs; apply via the SPI with an account access token.
official_mcp: Workable MCP Server (official, listed in the API reference nav — account-token, employer side)

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **partial** (public per-account jobs endpoint; apply is an account-token SPI call).
auth: 1. Public endpoints: no token — returns the account's public jobs.
2. SPI v3: Bearer access token generated in the company's Workable account (or a partner token / OAuth 2.0 for native partner integrations). A candidate cannot obtain one.

endpoints.notes: jobs[]: title, shortcode, code, state, department, url, application_url, shortlink, location{country,region,city,telecommuting}, created_at, description/requirements/benefits (with details)
full job incl. employment_type, industry, function, experience, education, salary

candidate{name, firstname, lastname, email, headline, summary, address, phone, cover_letter, education_entries[], experience_entries[], skills[], tags[], social_profiles[], resume_url or resume (base64), answers[]}, `sourced`, stage

reference.limits: A 'Rate limiting' page exists in the reference nav; the figure was not read. - Public jobs JSON is offered for careers-site embedding; everything that writes (candidates) is an employer-token API. Candidate-side apply → assist via `application_url`. Registry `api.apply: true` presumes the tenant owns the Workable account. - The registry `docs_url` (workable.readme.io/reference/job-board-api) is dead — use reference/accounts-1.
mcp_sdk: Workable MCP Server (official, listed in the API reference navigation; account token).

fields.name: api_token
fields.help: Workable API access token (Settings > Integrations > Apps / API access token) with the r_jobs scope; sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. It is the employer account's token.

config_fields.name: subdomain
config_fields.help: The Workable account subdomain, e.g. 'groove-tech' in https://groove-tech.workable.com.

me.note: GET /spi/v3/accounts/:subdomain 'Returns the specified account' (id, name, subdomain, description, url). Required scope: r_jobs.

search.note: Employer ATS API: GET /spi/v3/jobs?state=published lists the account's OWN published jobs (not a cross-company search). There is no keyword or location filter, so query/location are not sent — filter client-side. limit: 'By default results are limited to 50 … cannot be more than 100'. Paging is a since_id cursor (paging.next URL), which this tool does not follow: page is not sent, so only the first page is returned — raise limit to 100 for larger accounts. id is the job shortcode (use it with get_posting); salary_currency is lower-case (e.g. 'eur'); department, workplace_type, application_url, shortlink and location parts are in raw.

get_posting.note: GET /spi/v3/jobs/:shortcode 'will return the full job JSON object'; description is full_description (HTML); requirements, benefits, employment_type and application_url are in raw.

not_offered.apply: POST /jobs/:shortcode/candidates 'Creates a candidate at the specified job' with the employer's w_candidates token, i.e. an ATS import by the company, not a job seeker applying; candidates apply at the job's application_url.
not_offered.list_messages: The SPI v3 reference has no candidate messaging endpoints.

evidence: host groove-tech.workable.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Google Trust Services)
probe: 3/3 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 3/3 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; every parameter and body key named on the page
